ONE-ROUND REVISION — preserve the current working composition and implement these bounded changes in priority order:
1. Preserve and clarify intent: Keep the current title/menu composition and pixel-synthwave identity, but make all four highway lanes visibly continuous from horizon to receptors using subtle yet unmistakable separators. Keep every brief-required object, label, control, state, and relationship visible inside 1280×800; do not trade compliance for a cleaner crop.
2. Establish the reading structure: Keep the title as the first read, make Start the clear second read, and slightly reduce the sunset/demo-score cluster so attention then moves naturally into the highway. Reposition and rescale existing elements rather than deleting them; allow one primary focal region, one supporting information tier, and quiet utility controls.
3. Finish the shared system: Create a strict effects hierarchy: reserve the strongest glow for the hit line and active note, reduce background scanline/particle/grid opacity, and use one controlled chromatic offset on the title. Apply the correction through a small consistent set of palette, type, spacing, stroke, border, radius, shadow, and illustration rules, and repair visible clipping, collisions, weak contrast, or unfinished edges.
4. Add one content-specific expressive payoff: Tie each lane to a distinct instrument or dance cue through restrained symbols and note behaviors, integrate the title rhythmically with the highway perspective, and add one signature hit-line burst or dancer silhouette that makes this game recognizable beyond standard synthwave conventions. Limit this to the hero and semantically different states; reuse the system tokens and remove arbitrary decoration so it does not create a second competing focal point.
Implementation guardrails: edit the existing self-contained HTML/CSS/JS; use no remote assets, libraries, fonts, APIs, canvas packages, or network calls. Keep the fixed viewport at 1280×800 with no scrolling. Preserve all functioning content and verify small text, edge safety, and component alignment after the revision.
conflicts: Completeness versus hierarchy: retain the fidelity action—Keep the current title/menu composition and pixel-synthwave identity, but make all four highway lanes visibly continuous from horizon to receptors using subtle yet unmistakable separators.—while using the clarity action—Keep the title as the first read, make Start the clear second read, and slightly reduce the sunset/demo-score cluster so attention then moves naturally into the highway.—to tier, group, and rescale the required material instead of removing it.

System consistency versus expression: implement the craft action—Create a strict effects hierarchy: reserve the strongest glow for the hit line and active note, reduce background scanline/particle/grid opacity, and use one controlled chromatic offset on the title.—as the construction grammar, then permit the expressive action—Tie each lane to a distinct instrument or dance cue through restrained symbols and note behaviors, integrate the title rhythmically with the highway perspective, and add one signature hit-line burst or dancer silhouette that makes this game recognizable beyond standard synthwave conventions.—only as a bounded, content-motivated hero/state exception.

One-round scope versus accumulated requests: prioritize visible requirement ambiguity and the dominant craft defect first; apply secondary typography, spacing, and decorative refinements only when they reuse the same rules and do not trigger a rebuild.
rationale: The plan preserves every requested and already working element, lets hierarchy determine prominence, uses craft rules as the implementation substrate, and admits a single semantically motivated expressive exception so one revision remains coherent and feasible.
